note: tmgmt_deepl adds DeepL as a TMGMT translator via two @TranslatorPlugin plugins deepl_free and deepl_pro (shared base DeeplTranslator, ui DeeplTranslatorUi). A provider is a tmgmt_translator config entity (tmgmt.translator.<name>) with plugin deepl_free|deepl_pro and settings (schema tmgmt_deepl_settings: auth_key, url, url_usage, formality, split_sentences, tag_handling, ignore_tags, (non_)splitting_tags, preserve_formatting, outline_detection, auto_accept, test_url/test_url_usage). Configure route entity.tmgmt_translator.collection (/admin/tmgmt/translators); cron queue worker deepl_translate_worker; alter hooks + DeeplReceivedDataEvent; no permissions/Drush. Actual translation calls the DeepL API (needs an auth key), so ALL medium/hard cases are grounded in the tmgmt_translator config entity itself (creating/reading a provider and its settings does NOT call DeepL) using a placeholder auth_key; scripts create/delete their own tdeepl_* providers.

evals.prompt: What does the Drupal tmgmt_deepl module do, and which two translator options does it add to TMGMT?
evals.expected_output: It integrates the DeepL machine-translation API into TMGMT as translator providers, adding two translator plugins: deepl_free (DeepL API Free) and deepl_pro (DeepL API Pro).

evals.prompt: On a Drupal site, how do I set up DeepL translation with tmgmt_deepl - where do I add the provider and what do I need to enter?
evals.expected_output: Add a TMGMT translator/provider at /admin/tmgmt/translators (route entity.tmgmt_translator.collection), choose DeepL API Free or Pro, and enter your DeepL auth key (plus optional settings like formality). It is stored as a tmgmt_translator config entity.

evals.prompt: The tmgmt_deepl DeepL translator has a 'formality' setting. What values can it take and what does it control?
evals.expected_output: formality controls whether DeepL leans formal or informal. Values: default, more, less, prefer_more, prefer_less (the prefer_* options fall back to default when the target language does not support formality).

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a DeepL TMGMT translation provider configured. Inspect the live tmgmt translator configuration and tell me the value of its DeepL 'formality' setting.
evals.expected_output: formality is 'prefer_more': tmgmt.translator.tdeepl_known (plugin deepl_free) has settings.formality = prefer_more.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a DeepL translation provider named 'tdeepl_kind'. Inspect the live configuration: does it use the DeepL API Free or the DeepL API Pro plugin?
evals.expected_output: It uses DeepL API Pro: tmgmt.translator.tdeepl_kind has plugin: deepl_pro.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, add a TMGMT translation provider named 'tdeepl_task' that uses the DeepL API Free plugin (tmgmt_deepl). Apply the change to the live site. (A placeholder auth key is fine - do not attempt to contact DeepL.)
evals.expected_output: Create and save a tmgmt Translator config entity name tdeepl_task with plugin deepl_free. Verify checks tmgmt.translator.tdeepl_task exists with plugin deepl_free.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a DeepL translation provider 'tdeepl_ftask'. Configure it so DeepL produces more formal translations (set its formality to a formal option such as prefer_more). Apply the change to the live configuration.
evals.expected_output: Set tmgmt.translator.tdeepl_ftask settings.formality to 'prefer_more' (or 'more'). Verify checks formality is a formal option (more or prefer_more).
